$meta.title: Accurate stratigraphy for the Living Past Vol V cross-section
$meta.setting: Williston Basin margin, western North America, terminal Maastrichtian (~66 Ma). Land cliff = Hell Creek Formation (fluvial), unconformably over Fox Hills Sandstone (nearshore marine) and Pierre/Bearpaw Shale (offshore marine) at depth.
$meta.method: STRUCTURE is accurate + code-built (order, relative thickness, features); TEXTURE is MJ, one tile per lithology (see mjTexture). Never let MJ invent the layer order — that's the moat.
$meta.prewImpact_note: Scene is PRE-IMPACT (asteroid still in the sky). The K-Pg iridium layer / Z-coal boundary clay is deposited BY the impact, so it is deliberately ABSENT from the ground here. The living surface at top IS the latest-Cretaceous land surface.

features_legend.roots: root traces descending from a vegetated paleosol surface
features_legend.burrow: invertebrate/mammal burrow in a paleosol (CR09/CR12/CR13 habitat)
features_legend.egg_clutch: buried dinosaur nest (CR15) in a sandy overbank/levee paleosol
features_legend.ash: bentonite — altered volcanic ash from the scene's volcano (datable sanidine)
features_legend.unconformity: sharp erosive scour surface (up to ~3 m relief)

references: Hartman, Johnson & Nichols (eds.) 2002/2014, GSA Special Papers 361/503 — Hell Creek Formation & the K-Pg boundary
Fastovsky & Bercovici 2016, 'The Hell Creek Formation and its contribution to the K-Pg extinction: a short primer', Cretaceous Research
Flight/Belt et al.; Murphy et al. — Hell Creek lithostratigraphy, North Dakota (RG 279611040)
MDPI Geosciences 2020, 10(11):435 — Hell Creek sequence-stratigraphic review, Montana
USGS Geolex — Hell Creek Formation unit references
